reviewer: Claude research agent; no human review claimed
scope: Independent review of the 1,080 records of the HyInv batch (4 sources, 6 models, 1 method, 23 configurations, 1 benchmark, 8 datasets, 3 dataset subsets, 19 protocols, 485 evaluations, 498 results, 32 claims) and of the four concepts the batch adds to data/vocab/metric.ttl, by a different agent from the extractor, against the extraction frozen at commit 2da41a749f4b0d2c03076edab37086d824794ea6. All four pinned artifacts were re-downloaded at commit 0dcc533cc9f8f76c90ecbfe944df816b6672328a and their SHA-256 matched their source records; pdftotext -layout reproduced the archived text layer byte for byte (52ae9552b72266481b8c7190796f0bf2c93e4f8e84453c76b749b702edc50f52). npm run batch -- check-values was run over the whole batch against that text layer: of the 189 locators it can parse, 34 are in_cell and 155 in_row, with no not_in_row, wrong_column or overclaimed_in_row; the 309 figure and prose locators it cannot parse were checked separately. The 170 cells of Tables 6, 7, 8 and 9 and the 290 cells of the Figure 14 and Figure 15 numeric matrices were re-read by two reviewer scripts written for this pass, which find each row by its printed label and split the printed cells by position without using the extractor's parser: every printed value, numeric value and column matched, and the only printed cells of those tables and figures that the batch does not record are the 60 Figure 14 scTM cells that duplicate Table 6 at lower precision, the 10 dashes of the Native row and the 4 verdict cells of Table 9. Column assignment in Figure 14 was confirmed against the labelled columns of Table 2 (scTM, recovery and diversity blocks) and against Section 5.2's prose figures (diversity 0.331 on CATH4.3 test against 0.314 and 0.315, and 0.015 below ProteinZero V2 on RecentPDB); Figure 15's rests on its caption 'Same layout as Figure 14' and the rotated header fragments, with no independently labelled anchor. Table 1, the 8 Figure 4a bar labels and the 11 prose values were read by hand. A manual sample of 25 results was then drawn from the 498 with random.sample and seed 20261106 over the IDs in sorted order, and each was read by eye in the text layer with its row and column: 12 from Figure 15, 4 from Figure 14, 4 from Table 6, 3 from Table 1, 1 from Figure 4a and 1 from Section 6; all 25 matched, including column assignment. Every missing_metadata entry and the absence of uncertainty on 410 results were checked against the source; no record carries a null.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude research agent, independent of the extractor but not human scientific review. Transcription was checked against the pinned source; nothing was reproduced and no value was recomputed.

npm run batch -- check-values cannot parse a figure or prose locator, so 309 of the 498 results rest on the reviewer's own parse of the text layer and on the manual sample, not on the repository's checker.

The column order of the pLDDT, scRMSD and CA-lDDT blocks of Figure 15 (180 results) has no independently labelled anchor in the report. It follows the caption 'Same layout as Figure 14' and the rotated column-header fragments in the text layer, and is consistent with TS50 being the easiest panel in every block, but the report prints none of these 180 values anywhere else.

Appendix H says every number in the report is generated by scripts from result files, but neither the scripts nor the result files are published, so no cell can be recomputed from the released artifacts.
The report PDF is not archived in the batch. Its gzipped pdftotext -layout text layer is, and the PDF can be refetched at the pinned commit and checked against artifact_sha256.

A knowledge-graph build with the batch in the store found 126 live discrepancies and no finding naming a result of this batch; the three scoped evidence concerns withhold all 498 results from comparison and from discrepancy inference, so the batch's values are recorded and marked rather than compared.
